$comment: Vertical-slice art assets. Sizes are BASE-GRID pixels (480x270 canvas, shown x4 at 1080p). tools/codex/art.mjs generates each at native gpt-image size into art/raw/<id>.png and snaps it into godot/assets/<id>.png. Add an asset = add an entry here; the id is the file path under godot/assets/.
$keyComment: Transparent assets: Codex is told to use image_gen's real alpha; if it paints a backdrop instead, it must be this flat colour, which img.gd keys out automatically (auto-key only fires when the image has no real alpha). Override per asset with "key" when the subject contains that colour (e.g. the magenta lighter uses the default green; a plant would use "ff00ff").

kinds.scene: A full-frame environment layer. Paint it as a finished game background: every surface has material shading, the lighting is unified, nothing is a placeholder. Composition must leave the centre-bottom area (where a customer bust will stand in front of the counter) uncluttered enough that a character reads clearly against it.
kinds.portrait: A head-and-shoulders bust for dialogue, cut off cleanly at roughly the chest/upper-arm line as in Coffee Talk (the counter hides the rest). Facing the viewer, slight three-quarter allowed. Transparent background. Same pixel density and outline weight as the target-state reference so every cast member matches.
kinds.icon: A single tiny pixel icon drawn on a deliberately coarse grid: render it as a 16x16 (or the stated size) pixel-art icon scaled up to fill the canvas with big, crisp, uniform square pixels and no anti-aliasing, so it downsamples cleanly. Flat 3-5 colour palette, 1-px dark outline, readable silhouette.
kinds.prop: A single small object as a game sprite, transparent background, front/slightly-above view consistent with sitting on the counter, clean outline, Coffee Talk material shading.

assets.prompt:
TRUE PIXEL ART, NOT A SMOOTH ILLUSTRATION. Draw this as if a pixel artist placed every pixel on ONE locked grid at about 480x270 art pixels: chunky uniform square pixels, hard nearest-neighbour edges everywhere, 4-6 flat tones per material with stepped cluster shading, ordered dithering only for soft light falloff, clean 1-px dark outlines on every fixture. NO airbrushed glows, NO gaussian blur, NO anti-aliased or feathered edges, NO photographic glass reflections or sub-pixel glints, NO fine painterly noise, NO gradients. Every bottle, leaf and raindrop must be a deliberate cluster of a few pixels, not a rendered object.

SUBJECT: the interior of a Berlin Späti at night, seen from behind the counter (the shopkeeper's fixed side-on view: straight-on, at eye level, absolutely no isometric and no high angle), with NO people, NO counter and NO foreground objects — this is the flat back-wall layer that sits BEHIND a character bust.

FRAMING — the canvas is centre-cropped to 16:9 before use, so compose everything important inside the middle 16:9 band and treat the top ~15% and bottom ~15% of the canvas as expendable margin (ceiling darkness above, floor/plinth shadow below). Nothing readable may touch the top or bottom edge.

LEFT THIRD: a wall of drinks fridges seen through glass doors, cyan-white interior light, rows of generic bottles (green beer bottles with plain paper labels, yellow-label Mate-like bottles, water, cola-like). Keep the outer fridge casing dark and simple; simplify each shelf to a few repeated bottle silhouettes with low-contrast labels; reserve the brightest cyan-white for thin door-edge highlights only, so the fridges never out-shout the character.

MIDDLE THIRD: dark warm-brown vertical wood panelling, dressed but organised. The exact centre of the frame at head-and-chest height must stay CALM — plain panelling, no bright lamp, no poster, no glowing sign there. Around that calm pocket, to its left and right and above, hang flat kiosk fixtures in low contrast: a rack of abstract cigarette packs, small handwritten price cards, a row of key hooks, a little old radio, a taped-up notice, one narrow shelf of stand-in snacks and tobacco pouches. The hand-painted warm neon 'SPÄTI' sign glows HIGH in the LEFT of this middle band, sitting fully inside the 16:9 band with dark wood all around it and both umlaut dots drawn as two bright square pixel clusters so the word reads instantly.

RIGHT THIRD: the glass door and window onto the street — cold blue rainy Berlin night outside, wet pavement reflections in stepped bands, a distant magenta neon glow across the street, a bicycle silhouette, a small U-Bahn-style corner sign, a layered techno flyer and a few stickers taped to the inside of the glass (abstract shapes only, no readable text, no real logos), a hanging plant and a green-and-white football scarf (no real club) on a hook.

LIGHTING: two warm amber pendant lamps hang complete (whole shade visible, breathing room above) near the far left and far right; each pools a broad amber light shape with stepped cluster boundaries down its side of the room, leaving the middle dimmer. Warm highlight bands along shelf fronts and wood seams; a restrained cold blue rim on the edges facing the window. Compress the dark browns into two or three clear shadow families, not many near-blacks.

Dense but readable "wall of cozy stuff" like the Coffee Talk café, re-skinned as a Berlin kiosk; unified night lighting, warm amber interior against the cold blue window.

assets.$note: Transparent foreground strip. After keying/trimming it is fitted to 480 px wide (height ≈ 90–130) and the SceneLayers component bottom-aligns it, so the exact band height does not matter.
assets.prompt: The foreground counter band of a Berlin Späti seen from the shopkeeper's side, drawn as ONE wide horizontal strip that spans the FULL width of the canvas, edge to edge, and occupies only the BOTTOM 35% of the canvas. Straight-on eye-level view from just above the counter top, so a shallow band of the wooden surface is visible and the counter's front edge is perfectly horizontal and runs the whole width. A worn warm-brown wooden counter top with 4-5 tone wood grain running left to right and a bright amber lamp highlight along its front edge, and a darker wood front face below it falling off into shadow at the bottom of the canvas. Low, flat objects resting ON the counter, from left to right: a low plastic Pfand crate of stubby empty green bottles at the far left, a small ceramic coffee cup on a saucer left of centre, a mobile phone lying flat face-up near the centre, and a compact cash register at the far right. Keep every object low-profile: nothing may rise more than about one third of the strip height above the counter top, and nothing at all may be drawn in the top half of the canvas. The entire upper 65% of the canvas, everything above the counter and its objects, is empty background: transparent (real alpha), or one flat unshaded key colour if alpha is unavailable. Every edge where the counter or an object meets that background must be a hard, un-antialiased pixel edge with no glow, no soft fade and no coloured halo. No wall, no shelves, no people, no floor, no stools, no shadow cast onto the background.

Title-screen key art for the game: the exterior of a small Berlin Spaeti (corner kiosk) on a rainy night, seen straight on from across the street.

RENDER IT AS TRUE PIXEL ART, NOT A PAINTING. Draw a 480x270 pixel-art illustration and present it upscaled with nearest-neighbour so that every art pixel is a SOLID UNIFORM SQUARE BLOCK roughly 3 canvas pixels wide. Hard blocky edges everywhere, stepped diagonals, 1-pixel dark outlines on every shape. Absolutely no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft airbrush glow, no smooth gradients, no speckle/noise/grain/film texture, no photographic reflections. Shade with hand-placed clusters of 4-6 flat tones per material and a limited palette, dithering only for soft light falloff, exactly like the attached Coffee Talk references.

KEEP IT SIMPLE ENOUGH TO READ AT 480x270: few big shapes, a handful of hero props, generous dark masses. No crowd of tiny posters, no scattered micro-detail, no busy foliage. Puddles are broad flat horizontal bands of magenta and cyan reflection with a few stepped highlight steps, not wet photo-realism.

COMPOSITION (important): the shopfront occupies the LOWER TWO THIRDS of the frame. The UPPER-MIDDLE THIRD is deliberately calm and low-contrast - plain dark Berlin Altbau brick/stucco facade and rainy blue-black night sky, at most two small dim windows far to the sides - because a game title will be overlaid there. Nothing bright, no sign and no strong detail in that upper-middle area. The hand-painted warm neon SPAETI sign sits low, on the fascia directly above the shop window, small and wide. Keep all essential content inside the middle 84% of the canvas height (the top and bottom 8% will be cropped away). No large cropped objects at the left or right edges.

CONTENT: a lit shop window on each side of a central glass door, warm amber light spilling out onto wet cobblestones; inside, simple glowing drinks-fridge shelves with rows of plain bottle silhouettes (green beer bottles, yellow-label Mate-like bottles) in 2-4 flat tones; a plastic crate of empty bottles beside the door; a few stickers as flat coloured rectangles on the glass; a magenta and a cyan neon glow reflected in the street; rain as sparse straight light streaks. No real brands, no logos, no readable lettering anywhere except the single word on the sign.

THE PROTAGONIST: a lone young man standing on the pavement at the door, facing it, seen from behind at three-quarter with a sliver of his face visible. He must be clearly readable - about one third of the image height, a strong dark silhouette against the warm doorway light, with a warm amber rim light down his back and hair. He is exactly the man in reference image 1: messy wavy brown hair, a BRIGHT RED hoodie with the hood bunched at his neck, worn under an open brown-and-black jacket with a RED BAND across the sleeves, dark jeans. He holds a set of keys. Draw him with bold, clean shapes and a 1-pixel dark outline so the design reads at native resolution.

The protagonist 'You' (Onkel Cem's nephew) — EXACTLY the man in the target-state reference: mid-20s, messy wavy brown hair, light stubble, tired-but-earnest brown eyes, red hoodie under a brown/black layered jacket with a red band across the sleeves. Neutral, slightly guarded expression, hands out of frame. Head-and-shoulders bust for a dialogue portrait.

Lena, a broke Berlin art student in her early 20s: pale, freckled, reddish-auburn hair escaping from a dark green beanie, a paint-flecked oversized denim jacket over a striped top, a silver hoop earring, an empty Mate-like bottle held up near her shoulder as her signature prop. Neutral expression with a proud, slightly evasive set to the mouth. Head-and-shoulders bust for a dialogue portrait, Coffee Talk proportions and outline weight.
